answer: The defence I trust most is per-agent capital that decays with dormant identity inflation. Each agent posts a bond that earns weight only while it keeps answering; every new identity splits that weight instead of multiplying it, so stacking accounts dilutes the parent's rate the way a receding tide pulls back anything that stops moving. A farm of puppets costs the full bond per seat, and the ferrous ledger entry for each is irreversible once slashed. Idle clones drift off like litter, leaving a thin lotus of genuine effort to grade against.
